title: Payloads per role of a2dlc run (what goes inside role-request.payload and role-response.payload)
description: Each block of the build order (ADR meta/0004, amendment 2026-10-17) adds its role's payload here. role-request and role-response require them per role with if/then. Block 2: the Saboteur. Block 3: the Builder (Tier 0). Block 5: the live mutants of Stage 5 in the Saboteur's request (survivors). Block 6: the specifiers and the Inquisitor of Stage 1. Block 7: the Back-translator and the Inquisitor comparator of Stage 1.5.

saboteur_request.description: Stage 4, adversarial loop over uncovered_change, and Stage 5, over the live mutants (survivors): the core tells it which changed lines nobody examined and where the tests have to live. What it can read is in /in (contract S*, public signatures, escalations, intent); never the builder's code.

uncovered.description: Stage 4: uncovered lines. In Stage 5 it is empty and the request brings survivors; one of the two cannot be empty.

tests_paths.description: Globs of config.tests.paths: a test outside them is not accepted (it could not overwrite a source through the overlay).

command.description: config.tests.command, so the role knows which runner and convention run the tests.

previous_tests.description: Tests that the Saboteur already delivered in earlier rounds and remain in the overlay: no need to repeat them.

survivors.description: Block 5, Stage 5: mutants that survived T with the kill gate under the threshold. The Saboteur writes tests that kill them, against the signatures and the contract: the description states the operator and the line, never the candidate's code (§5, "no implementation comments").

saboteur_response.description: With status ok: the test files it wrote to /out/tests/<path>, with the path they will have in the repo and their hash. The core copies them to the run's overlay only if the hash matches and the path matches tests_paths; targets is what the role says it attacked (a declaration, not proof).

builder_request.description: Block 3. Stage 3, Tier 0 loop: the Builder works in /work (a writable copy of the run's base, without .git) and the core takes the state of /work at the end of each round as the candidate. It sees the same as /in (S*, blocked probes, Tier 0 feedback, and the intent whenever it exists, with or without S*: a deviation from §3 declared in the deviations table of the README); never the Saboteur's suite nor another Builder's /work.

intent.description: Content of the run's intent.json, or null if there is none.

contract.description: S* (contract.json), or null in lite mode.

probes.description: Blocked probes of S* (probes.json): Tier 0 runs against /work those that carry file and expr; null if the run has none.

tier0_feedback.description: What Tier 0 gave on /work in the previous round (engine-tier0-response, summed across engines); null in the first.

header.description: @a2dlc header values (§6.3) that each created or modified source file must declare. The core builds them; the Builder copies them.

boundary.description: CB-04: what the intent declares untouchable (forbidden_paths, do_not_refactor). Absent if the intent declares no boundary; the builder does not change it and, if it does, the stage escalates.

engine_language.description: Engine language of the repo. Absent means python.

paradigm.description: Programming paradigm the builder follows (roles.<role>.paradigm). Prompt-enforced, not verified.

critical.description: True when the effective track of the router is critical (N=2): the builder prompt then asks for lemmas.

builder_header.description: @a2dlc header (§6.3) of the run for the Builder. slice_id, mode and contract_hash are what Stage 3 compares with each changed source file; a file that declares others fails the stage. contract_hash is null without S* (lite mode). protected_invariants comes from intent.invariants; rejected_alternatives from intent.rejected_alternatives; do_not_refactor stays empty until the intent has boundary.do_not_refactor.

builder_response.description: With status ok: a summary and the files it says it touched. It is a declaration, not proof: the candidate is the /work tree, and the core reads nothing else from /out.

lemmas.description: Optional, Critical slices (N=2): the pure internal functions the builder declares with their postconditions. Names are unique within the array (the core checks it).

saboteur_survivor.description: Block 5: a live mutant as the Saboteur sees it (no id or code: file, line, operator and the template description).

spec_discrepancy.description: Block 6. A point where S_α and S_β do not say the same thing, with what each one says. resolution null: the Inquisitor could not decide it with the intent and the catalogue; after --max-spec-rounds it escalates (spec_divergence).

topic.description: Function, error or assumption on which they diverge (e.g. media: empty list).

specifier_request.description: Block 6, Stage 1 (greenfield, brownfield_facade): Specifier α or β translates the intent into a candidate contract. It sees the intent and, if it exists, the capture (§3); never the other one's contract nor code from other slices. From round 2 onward it brings the discrepancies the Inquisitor did not resolve.

engine_language.description: Engine language of the repo. Absent means python.

rejection.description: Only on the retry of the same round: why the core rejected the previous answer (a payload out of contract, a contract that does not validate, a wrong source or slice_id). Absent on the first attempt.

specifier_response.description: With status ok: the candidate contract. source must be the responding role and slice_id the run's; the core saves it as contract_alpha.json or contract_beta.json.

inquisitor_request.description: Block 6, Stage 1: the two candidates and the base's assumption catalogue (null if the repo has none). Neither builder code nor the Saboteur's tests.

engine_language.description: Engine language of the repo. Absent means python.

rejection.description: Only on the retry of the same round: why the core rejected the previous answer (an invented catalogue id, a missing consensus probe, a contract that does not validate). Absent on the first attempt.

inquisitor_response.description: With status ok: consensus S*, the discrepancies it found (with their resolution or null) and the assumptions left open for a person. Each assumption with source catalogue must cite a catalogue entry.

back_translator_request.description: Block 7, Stage 1.5: the Back-translator reads S* in /in/contract.json and nothing else (§3: neither the intent nor the specifiers' reasoning). contract_hash is the sha256 of that file, to tie the translation to the translated contract.

back_translator_response.description: With status ok: what the slice does according to S*, in prose, and concrete assertions (an input and what happens, or what S* forbids). The core saves it as backtranslation.json.

inquisitor_bt_request.description: Block 7, Stage 1.5: the Inquisitor as comparator of the back-translation (§5 step 5). It receives the intent and the translation in the payload, not via /in: the §3 policy is per role, and mounting intent.json for the Inquisitor would also show it in Stage 1. The prompt is chosen by request.stage (section "Stage 1.5" of roles/prompts/inquisitor.md).

inquisitor_bt_response.description: With status ok: whether the translation says the same as the intent and, if not, each difference (what the intent says, what S* implies). matches true goes without discrepancies.

propose_request.description: Stage propose (a2dlc propose): the Propose role reads the public signatures of the changed functions and the diff, and proposes properties for them.

engine_language.description: Engine language of the repo that produced the signatures.

diff.description: Unified diff of the changed files.

propose_response.description: With status ok: the properties proposed for the changed functions. Each one names its target, the property in prose and the file where it belongs.
